questions.def: 'Not until' requires a time expression; 'later' is correct.
questions.question: It wasn't until ___ that I understood the problem.

questions.def: 'What' clause focuses on the need; 'most' emphasizes degree.
questions.question: What I need ___ is a vacation.

questions.def: 'Overstress' emphasizes the importance; 'cannot' intensifies.
questions.question: ___ the importance of regular exercise.

questions.def: 'As' after an adjective shows concession and emphasis.
questions.question: ___ he may be, he still needs help.

questions.def: Corrects a misinterpretation; 'not' is standard negation.
questions.question: It is ___ the money that motivates him.

questions.def: With 'it', 'were' should be 'was' for a singular subject.
questions.question: It were him who called last night.

questions.def: 'Underscores' subtly emphasizes a point, more formal.
questions.question: The report ___ the need for more funding.

questions.def: 'Not only' inverts subject/auxiliary for emphasis.
questions.question: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot his keys.

questions.def: 'What' clause acts as a singular subject; requires 'is'.
questions.question: What ___ important is that we act now.

questions.def: 'Drew attention to' focuses on guiding the audience's focus.
questions.question: The speaker ___ the key issues.

questions.def: 'Such' emphasizes the degree of the adjective 'beautiful'.
questions.question: ___ a beautiful day that we decided to go to the beach.

questions.def: After 'was', use the subject pronoun 'she'.
questions.question: It was ___ who broke the vase.

questions.def: 'Never' inverts subject/auxiliary: 'have I seen'.
questions.question: Never I have seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.def: 'Centered' implies a primary and deliberate focus.
questions.question: The discussion ___ primarily on environmental issues.

questions.def: 'Little' inverts subject/auxiliary for emphasis.
questions.question: Little ___ that he was being watched.

questions.def: 'That' is correct relative pronoun for emphasis.
questions.question: It is the environment ___ we must protect.

questions.def: 'Reiterated' formally emphasizes repeated commitment.
questions.question: The company ___ its commitment to sustainability.

questions.def: 'Hardly' inverts subject/auxiliary for emphasis.
questions.question: Hardly ___ the house when it started to rain.

questions.def: Emphasis on 'never' with inversion of possessive.
questions.question: It was ___ intention to cause any trouble.

questions.def: Inversion needed: 'So important was the matter...'
questions.question: So important the matter was that we acted immediately.

questions.def: 'Hammered home' idiomatically emphasizes a point.
questions.question: The teacher ___ the importance of practice.

questions.def: 'Only then' inverts subject/auxiliary for emphasis.
questions.question: Only then ___ how serious the situation was.

questions.def: 'This point' focuses on the specific disagreement.
questions.question: It is ___ that I disagree with.

questions.def: 'Geared' implies a designed focus or direction.
questions.question: The new law ___ on reducing pollution.

questions.def: 'At no time' inverts subject/auxiliary for emphasis.
questions.question: At no time ___ to deceive anyone.

questions.def: 'The underlying issue' specifically highlights the central problem.
questions.question: It is ___ that needs to be addressed.

questions.def: 'It wasn't until...' requires 'later' to express a time delay.
questions.question: It wasn't until ___ that she understood the problem.

questions.def: The subject is 'what she needs,' a singular concept taking 'is'.
questions.question: What she needs ___ a good night's sleep.

questions.def: Simple past tense is correct to focus on a completed action.
questions.question: The speaker ___ the importance of education.

questions.def: 'As' in this structure requires the adjective before: Rich as he may be.
questions.question: ___ he may be, he still needs guidance.
